newsitem.title: JAPAN: MOF, JSDA aim for shorter JGB settlement period.
newsitem.headline: MOF, JSDA aim for shorter JGB settlement period.

text.p: A Ministry of Finance official and an official for the Japan Securities Dealers' Association (JSDA) said on Friday they are aiming to further shorten the settlement period for Japanese government bonds (JGBs).
"At the earliest, we would like to start 'T plus three' in April 1997," Kaname Seki, vice-chairman of the Japan Securities Dealers' Association, told Reuters Financial Television.
Under a "T plus three" system, deliveries of JGBs take place three business days after the transaction date.
Japan has just shortened the settlement period to "T plus seven" for JGB transactions made from September 19.

Hiromichi Tanigawa, director of the MOF securities bureau's bond market office, said shorter settlement periods were desirable, because there would be less chance of unpredictable events occuring before settlement.
"Unpredictable events which take place in the time between trade and settlement can lead to unexpected risk," Tanigawa said.
Examples of such unpredictable events would be earthquakes, or sudden bankruptcy on the part of trading counterparts, he said.
